name: Texas

regulator.name: Texas Secretary of State, Registrations Unit

law.name: Texas athlete agent law (Occupations Code ch. 2051)

covers_nil_agents: Unclear. Educ. Code 51.9246 uses this act's agent definition for NIL, but the act is written for pro and financial services deals. Ask the Secretary of State if NIL-only agents must register.
summary: Register with the Secretary of State every year. $500 plus a $50,000 bond.
contract_warning:
This athlete agent is registered with the Secretary of State of the State of Texas. Registration with the Secretary of State does not imply approval or endorsement by the Secretary of State of the competence of the athlete agent or of the specific terms and conditions of this contract.
Do not sign this contract until you have read it or if it contains blank spaces.
If you decide that you do not wish to purchase the services of the athlete agent, you may cancel this contract by notifying the athlete agent in writing of your desire to cancel the contract not later than the 16th day after the date on which you sign this contract. You may not waive the right to cancel this contract. If you cancel this contract within 16 days, you are not required to pay any consideration under the contract or return any consideration received.
You may lose your eligibility to compete as an athlete in your sport. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility.
If you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after entering into this contract both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director.

steps.text: Fill out Form 2501, Application for Registration
steps.detail: Add Form 2506 for each financially interested party and Form 2507 contact sheet.

steps.text: Get a $50,000 surety bond (Form 2504)
Add a $100,000 financial services bond or affidavit
steps.detail: Form 2503 bond if you give financial services, otherwise Form 2502 affidavit.

steps.text: Pro sports only: get players' association certification
steps.detail: Not needed for limited agents in sports like golf or tennis.

steps.text: Pay $500
steps.detail: Fees aren't refunded unless the state denies you.

steps.text: Mail it to the Registrations Unit
Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Use a contract form approved by the Secretary of State
steps.detail: Copy the required notice into it without changes.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your fees and how they're figured, other pay you get for the deal, services, anyone else being paid, expenses, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the state's notice in the contract so it stands out
steps.detail: Use at least 10-point type in bold, capitals or underline. Use the exact words in the warning box.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy when they sign
steps.detail: The Texas sections we read don't list this, but it's good practice.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: The contract notice says you and the athlete both must. The athlete may cancel in writing within 16 days.

steps.text: Send the athletic director a copy of the contract within 10 days
steps.detail: Do this if the athlete is a college student.

steps.text: If an athlete or their family asks to meet, tell the athletic director before the meeting
steps.detail: You may mail info about yourself to an athlete only if you send the athletic director a copy at the same time.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: State law (Occ. Code 2051.351) and federal law (SPARTA) both ban pre-dating or post-dating it.

steps.text: File a copy of each contract with the Secretary of State within 10 days of signing
steps.detail: If your fees change later, file the new version too.

steps.text: Keep client records
steps.detail: Names and addresses, fees paid, services, contracts, recruiting costs, and travel and entertainment spending. Give the state copies if it asks.

steps.text: Never give anything of value to an athlete or their family before their last college game
steps.detail: Also never lie, pay school staff for referrals, or contact athletes in ways the law doesn't allow.

steps.text: Put your name and address in all your ads
Renew every year with Form 2505 and pay $500
steps.detail: Registration lasts 1 year. You can renew up to 60 days before it ends.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: Texas law doesn't say how many years to keep records (Occ. Code 2051.352). Ask the Secretary of State Registrations Unit.

Statute text was read on texas.public.law (marked up to date May 26, 2025) because the official site wouldn't load. Check the 2051.204 notice wording on statutes.capitol.texas.gov before you print contracts.
